site.name: github-404
site.summary: github-404-clone Clone of the GitHub 404 error page. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | 404 page: top GitHub nav bar, centered error message ("This is not the web page you are looking for."), Octocat illustration, links to home / search / contact support | | `style.css` | Dark background, illustration styling, buttons | | `app.js` | Illustration hover / parallax effect, (optional) fake search suggestions |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full github-404 system, prioritizing the primary error page flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The github-404 system provides a robust single-page application experience, effectively integrating mock search, support, and system status views. However, the user experience is hampered by several interactive blind spots, most notably a main logo that fails basic navigation and accessibility expectations. Additionally, mobile usability is degraded by consistently undersized touch targets across the header and interactive forms, while misleading affordances on static content and a lack of empty-state validation in the search flow create minor friction points.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the GitHub 404 page clone, focusing on interactive elements, visual fidelity, and responsive layout.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will sequentially validate all functional areas of the single-page 404 clone. It will begin with top navigation and footer links, proceed to test the central search mechanism and adjacent category buttons, and conclude with a mobile viewport evaluation to address identified tap-target warnings.
assumptions: Most navigation and footer links are placeholders pointing to '#'.
The search functionality may not perform a real search but might trigger fake suggestions or UI state changes.
risk_hotspots: Empty accessibility label on the primary GitHub logo link (ux-1).
Search input (ux-5) and Search button (ux-6) interaction and potential JS-driven fake suggestions.
Widespread small tap targets across top nav, category buttons, and footer links.

phases.title: Navigation and Layout Validation
phases.objective: Verify the functionality of top navigation and footer links, and check the structural layout.
key_checks: Click the unlabelled logo link (ux-1) to see where it routes.
Click 'Search' (ux-2), 'Support' (ux-3), and 'Status' (ux-4) in the top nav.
Verify the 'contact support' (ux-10) and 'GitHub Status' (ux-11) links at the bottom.
exit_criteria: All header and footer links have been interacted with and their destination or lack thereof is confirmed.

phases.title: Search Mechanism Testing
phases.objective: Test the central search input and its submission.
key_checks: Type a test query into 'Search GitHub' (ux-5) and observe if any fake search suggestions appear.
Click the green 'Search' button (ux-6) and check if it submits a form or alters the URL.
Press 'Enter' while focused on the search input.
exit_criteria: Search input accepts text, and form submission behavior is documented.

phases.title: Category Buttons Interaction
phases.objective: Validate the behavior of the buttons located below the search bar.
exit_criteria: All three category buttons have been clicked to see if they act as filters, links, or visual toggles.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Assessment
phases.objective: Evaluate the page layout and usability on a mobile viewport, focusing on the small tap target layout warnings.
key_checks: Assess if the top navigation collapses into a hamburger menu or if it cramps the screen.
Re-evaluate the interactability of the category buttons (ux-7, ux-8, ux-9) and footer links.
exit_criteria: Mobile viewport screenshot captured and layout structure analyzed for usability issues.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise all navigation links, the search input, submit button, and category filters.
coverage_targets.mobile: Switch to mobile viewport to specifically test the layout of the flagged small tap targets.

notes: The readme mentions a parallax/hover effect on the illustration; note any visual changes during mouse movements or interactions if the framework captures them.

findings.user_goal: Navigate back to the homepage or identify the site via screen reader.
findings.problem: The top-left GitHub logo link lacks an accessible label and its `href` is set to `#`, meaning it does not navigate the user anywhere.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag the logo (`ux-1`) with an `empty_interactive_label`. Session memory notes that clicking the logo fails the common expectation of returning to the homepage.
findings.why_it_matters: Users rely on the site logo as a universal 'escape hatch' to return to the root homepage. For screen reader users, an empty link label announces as 'link' with no context, completely hiding the site identity.
findings.suggestion: Add an `aria-label="GitHub homepage"` or visually hidden text to the logo link, and update the `href` to point to the actual homepage path (e.g., `/` or `index.html`) rather than `#`.

findings.user_goal: Interact with site navigation and submit forms easily on a touch device.
findings.problem: Multiple primary interactive elements fall significantly below the recommended 44x44px minimum touch target size for mobile devices.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings and session memory indicate that the header navigation links ('Search', 'Support', 'Status') have a vertical height of 24px. The logo is 32x32px, category filter buttons are 38px high, and form submit/subscribe buttons are 36-38px high.
findings.why_it_matters: Undersized tap targets lead to accidental misclicks, frustration, and a degraded experience for users on mobile devices or those with motor impairments.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding on header links, filter tabs, and form buttons to ensure they have a minimum interactive area of 44x44px on mobile viewports.
findings.source_hint: Header nav links (ux-2, ux-3, ux-4), Subscribe button (ux-47)

findings.user_goal: Expand incident history entries to read more details.
findings.problem: Incident history cards mimic interactive buttons but are completely static, failing to expand or collapse when clicked.
findings.evidence: Elements like 'Degraded performance for Codespaces' and 'Intermittent API errors' have `role="button"`, but testing (Steps 13-18, 19-24, and 49) confirmed that clicking them does not trigger any state change or toggle details; the text is statically visible at all times.
findings.why_it_matters: Assigning interactive roles to static content creates a false affordance, confusing users who expect the interface to respond to their clicks.
findings.suggestion: If the incident details are meant to be permanently visible, remove the `role="button"` attribute and any hover/focus styling that implies interactivity. If they are meant to be accordions, implement the expand/collapse JavaScript logic.

findings.problem: Submitting an empty search query results in no visible system response or validation feedback.
findings.evidence: Session memory (Steps 25-30) notes: 'Clicking the Search button with an empty input field yields no visible response or validation message, leaving users without clear feedback.'
findings.why_it_matters: Without feedback, users may wonder if the search button is broken or if the page is simply loading slowly.
findings.suggestion: Disable the search button when the input is empty, or provide a brief, visible validation message (e.g., 'Please enter a search term') when an empty submission is attempted.
